title: Research Analyst/Senior Research Analyst - Frontier AI Policy
description:
RAND Europe is an independent, not-for-profit research organisation whose mission is to help improve policy and decision-making through rigorous and independent research and analysis. We benefit the public interest through the impact and wide dissemination of over 200 projects per year. Our work at its most impactful changes policy, practice and process to the benefit of the public good. That is also our organisational mission.

RAND Europe has approximately 200 staff across offices in Cambridge, Brussels, and the Hague. Our staff represents 22 nationalities, speaks over 20 languages and covers 31 academic disciplines. Our multi- and inter-disciplinary approaches to research generate unique perspectives and insights for our wide-ranging government, foundation and other NGO clients.

We wish to recruit an Analyst/Senior Analyst in our Science and Emerging Technology team (SET) to support our growing portfolio of frontier AI policy research, with additional opportunities to get involved in the SET team’s broader portfolio of policy research in research and innovation systems, emerging technology and energy and environment.

The Science and Emerging Technology (SET) group at RAND Europe conducts a wide-ranging portfolio of policy research for a diverse client base in the UK, Europe and beyond. Our work covers:

- Emerging technology policy: Analysis of the trends, applications and impacts of new and emerging technologies from artificial intelligence and biotechnology to quantum technology and virtual reality, using a variety of quantitative and qualitative methods. This includes examining the societal and policy implications of technologies across sectors and a broad set of areas such as biosecurity, technology oversight, trust and ethics public engagement, and work and skills. See: https://www.rand.org/randeurope/research/science-technology-innovation/digital.html
- Research and innovation policy: Analysis of research and innovation systems including how they work and how they can be improved. This includes evaluations of portfolios of R&I, research strategy development, landscape reviews, and metascience research (including topics like scientometrics, AI in science, researcher mobility, researcher wellbeing and open science). See: https://www.rand.org/randeurope/research/science-technology-innovation/science-of-science.html
- Energy and environment policy: Energy and energy innovation, climate risk and policy, food systems and strategy, green jobs and skills, transport, and futures analysis of environment and sustainability issues. See: https://www.rand.org/randeurope/research/science-technology-innovation/environmental-sustainability-and-climate-change.html

This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the world’s most respected public policy research organisations and contribute to pioneering work at the intersection of AI and other emerging technologies.

Frontier AI is increasingly relevant to economic competitiveness, national security, public services, scientific progress and international stability. Concern over frontier capabilities have led to a large and growing body of evaluations and measurement techniques. Yet the institutions responsible for governing its development and deployment often lack clear ways to interpret technical evidence, determine what assurance claims can be relied upon, or act when systems create risks across organisational, sectoral or national boundaries.

RAND Europe is building a Frontier AI Policy function to address this gap.

The function examines how evidence from AI testing, measurement, evaluation and monitoring becomes sufficiently credible, interpretable and context-specific to support real-world decisions. These decisions include whether systems should be developed, deployed, procured, regulated, assured, insured, constrained or coordinated internationally.

The successful candidate will contribute to research at the intersection of frontier-AI capabilities, AI safety and security, institutional design and public policy. They will work with technical researchers, policymakers, regulators, standards and assurance bodies, public procurers, industry, civil society and international partners.

The role is not limited to commentary on AI regulation, nor to technical model evaluation. It sits at the interface between them: understanding what technical evidence establishes, what uncertainty remains, who can rely on it, and what institutional action should follow.

Relevant areas of work may include:

- Policy frameworks around frontier-AI measurement, testing, evaluation and assurance;

- AI safety, security, misuse and systemic-risk governance;

- regulatory capacity, public procurement and deployment governance;

- AI in critical infrastructure, financial services, public administration and other high-consequence settings;

- incident reporting, monitoring, crisis preparedness and tabletop exercises;

- standards, conformity assessment, accreditation and technical governance;

- liability, insurance and accountability across AI value chains;

- middle-power agency, international coordination, verification and strategic preparedness.

This role offers the opportunity to help shape a growing research programme at an unusually consequential moment for AI policy.

Responsibilities

- Contribute to or manage interdisciplinary projects assessing the national and international policy implications of AI advances.

- Lead or co-lead research tasks on frontier-AI governance, assurance, institutional readiness, international coordination or related topics.

- Develop research designs and grant applications using mixed methods, including literature review, interviews, document analysis, comparative policy analysis, expert elicitation, scenario analysis and workshops or tabletop exercises.

- Analyse how technical findings from AI testing, evaluation, red teaming and monitoring should inform institutional decisions.

- Support the management of relationships with external partners, collaborators and clients.

- Contribute to the development of RAND Europe’s frameworks for decision-ready evidence, AI assurance, regulatory capacity and frontier-AI preparedness.

- Represent RAND Europe in workshops, consultations, meetings and external events.

- Working with team members and the Research Group Director to develop SET’s research and strategy.

- Working in a collegiate manner and contributing to the development and profile of the wider organisation.

- Helping to raise RAND Europe’s profile and communicate research findings to maximise impact.

Requirements

- A strong interest in assessing AI capabilities, understanding AI safety and security risks, and advancing policies and frameworks for the responsible governance of AI and other high‑consequence technologies.
- The ability to engage critically with evidence from AI testing, evaluation, red teaming, monitoring or related technical work, including understanding its scope, limitations and policy relevance.

- Demonstrable experience in developing original research proposals and frameworks and seeing these through into successful publications (or other outputs)

- A background or strong familiarity with one or more of the following domains: AI safety, AI security, AI for good, AI regulation, AI assurance, legislative approaches to AI, computer engineering, science and technology policy.

- Excellent analytical, writing and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

- Experience working collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams, ideally spanning technical and policy domains.

- An awareness of the AI Governance organisational landscape, including key grantmakers and potential collaborators.
- Familiarity with AI models, machine-learning concepts or computational tools is desirable, but deep technical ML expertise is not required.
- Experience with Python, R, data analysis or other computational methods is desirable where relevant to the candidate’s research background, but not essential.

- A commitment to RAND Europe’s core values of quality, objectivity, collaboration, service and learning.

Personal qualities:

- Curiosity and adaptability, with enthusiasm for working at the frontier of AI policy research.

- Motivated by the importance of frontier-AI risks and opportunities, while remaining open-minded, evidence-led and non-advocacy-driven

- Comfortable with uncertainty, able to distinguish evidence from speculation, state limitations clearly and develop useful analysis even where information is incomplete.

- Proactive and self-motivated, with the ability to work independently and as part of a team.

- Strategic thinker, capable of linking technical findings to broader policy and security implications.

- Strong communicator, able to explain complex analyses clearly and persuasively to diverse audiences.

- Collaborative and collegial, fostering a supportive team culture and sharing expertise openly.

- Commercially and policy aware, with the ability to identify emerging opportunities for impact and growth.

- Open-minded and intellectually humble, receptive to learning from colleagues across disciplines and levels of seniority.

This role will be based in RAND Europe’s Cambridge office, working alongside RAND Europe colleagues, though we have a hybrid working model with the option to work mostly from home (minimum of one day per week in the office on average, with some flexibility). There will also be some requirement to travel and spend brief periods away visiting clients on site – typically in London and Brussels though occasionally further afield.

Salary

Analyst - Starting salary from £33,000 per annum depending on experience

Senior Analyst - Starting salary from £41,000 per annum depending on experience

Benefits

- Pension - 8% Employer contribution;
- 33 days holiday allowance, including the Bank Holidays;
- Annual salary review;
- BUPA medical insurance;
- Generous company sick pay;
- Enhanced family friendly policies;
- Group income protection scheme;
- Group life assurance;
- Compassionate leave;
- Flexible working arrangements;
- Learning and development opportunities;
- Employee wellbeing training and support;
- Fresh fruit every day;
- Free on-site parking;
- Cycle to work scheme;
- Access to company bikes;
- Service awards.

Application

If you believe you are suited to the above role, please submit an application comprising of a CV and covering letter below by 8th November 2026. If you have not been contacted within 30 days of application deadline, please assume your application has not been successful.

title: Senior Analyst - Space - Defence, Security and Justice
description:
RAND is a not-for-profit research institute with over 30 years of experience in conducting policy research for governments, international organisations, research councils, charitable foundations, and other organisations. We believe that good research helps shape sound answers to pressing societal challenges, ultimately making communities safer and more secure, healthier and more prosperous in the future. RAND Europe has offices in Cambridge, Brussels and The Hague and employs approximately 200 staff.

We wish to recruit an experienced Senior Analyst in Space Security within our Defence, Security and Justice (DSJ) research group, to contribute to the growth of the RAND Europe Space Hub (RESH). The focus of this role is to help facilitate our growing portfolio of space-related research for governmental clients, with a particular focus on space security, space programmatic and portfolio evaluations, and wider space policy, governance, regulatory or capability issues.

The DSJ research group conducts a wide-ranging portfolio of research for a diverse client base in the UK, Europe and beyond. Our clients include UK government departments and agencies (e.g. Ministry of Defence, Home Office, FCDO, DSIT, UK Space Agency), other national governments (e.g. Dutch), EU institutions (e.g. European Commission, EDA, European Parliament), and international defence and security organisations (e.g. NATO, United Nations), and various third sector and humanitarian organisations.

Our work covers a broad range of public policy issues across:

- Defence (defence strategy, policy, capability, and acquisition; defence economics; defence workforce and Armed Forces community)
- Security (terrorism; counter-violent extremism; human security; border security; energy security; resilience and cyber)
- Criminal Justice (rehabilitation and preventing crime; organised crime; law enforcement cooperation; drugs and illicit markets)

DSJ researchers also participate in the RAND Europe Space Hub (RESH), a cross-RAND centre of excellence for space-related research, analysis and wargaming. This cross-cutting hub involves ~15 RAND staff and draws both on the defence and security-focused space expertise and the civil and commercial space expertise of its’ members.

The successful applicant will contribute to business development and project delivery for our portfolio of space research. We are looking for an individual with experience of winning, designing and delivering space-related projects for national governments and militaries in the UK and Europe and/or for international organisations (e.g. EU, ESA, NATO). In particular, experience working with ESA and/or evaluation expertise is a plus.

We are looking for an individual with a keen interest and understanding of civil and defence space issues; space strategy, policy, governance and regulatory issues more broadly, both at the national and international level; and trends in space capabilities, technologies and industry. Ideally, you will have experience of employing a variety of research and analysis methods, including quasi-experimental design, as part of a multi-method approach to dealing with complex space-related challenges. You will also be experienced at leading and managing the delivery of projects, working with a team of researchers and must have strong analysis skills.

Key Responsibilities

Research Management

- Managing RAND Europe’s successful research track record in space security and space policy issues, and supporting the delivery of a varied portfolio of research projects and expanding into new areas of work.
- Contributing to the group’s thought leadership on space and the wider implications of the space domain for civil, defence and security policy issues.
- Mentoring more junior research staff and facilitating the development of others’ project management, leadership and methodological skills.
- Helping ensure that RAND Europe’s research has a positive impact within policy communities and the wider world.
- Engaging with the RAND US’s Space Enterprise Initiative (RSEI) to leverage the expertise available across RAND’s global footprint, as well as playing a collaborative role in the RAND Europe Space Hub (RESH).

Business development

- Contributing to and supporting the delivery of DSJ group revenue and sales targets by helping secure funding for research and consultancy tasks.
- Co-ordinating, managing and supporting a portfolio of business development initiatives including supporting bid and proposal activity – in particular relating to our space portfolio.
- Building networks and contacts with funders and collaborators.

Group and other responsibilities

- Working with team members to deliver the group’s strategic objectives.
- Working in a collegiate manner and contributing to the development and profile of the wider organisation.
- Helping to raise RAND Europe’s profile and communicate research findings to maximise impact.

Requirements

- Demonstrable experience in leading/managing the design and delivery of space-related research. Ideally candidates will have experience of delivering projects for national governments, militaries or space agencies in the UK/EU.
- Demonstrable experience in using a variety of research methods to inform policy on space security, defence and policy issues, and a proven ability to articulate the value of research in a defence and security context.
- Experience of integrating multiple research and analysis methods as part of multi-method approaches to problem solving and/or policy research.

- Experience of winning and delivering research projects for UK, European or international defence organisations and funders.
- Strong networks of professional connections across the space security, defence, and policy community in the UK, Europe and further afield.
- Evidence of working as part of a team, motivating others, mentoring and actively developing colleagues for skills and career progression.
- Excellent analytical, writing and presentation skills (evidenced by examples) and the proven ability to communicate effectively with clients and to varied internal and external audiences. You should have demonstrable experience of writing, editing and disseminating the findings of research to policy audiences.
- Strong project leadership / management experience, including experience of people management, stakeholder management and budgeting.
- Proven ability to distil complex information and engage with detail whilst considering bigger picture issues and to message research and analysis findings clearly, succinctly and in consideration of target audiences.
- Eligible for, and willing to obtain, relevant national (e.g., UK) and/or NATO security clearance where required as part of the role.

Personal qualities

title: Senior Quantitative Evaluation Roles - Social Policy
description:
RAND Europe is an independent, not-for-profit research organisation whose mission is to help improve policy and decision-making through rigorous and independent research and analysis. Our methods are typically rooted in the social sciences – members of the Health and Care research group have backgrounds in health services research; health economics; epidemiology; public health; psychology; health innovation; sociology and other social science and health related disciplines.

About the roles

RAND Europe is a leading provider of complex policy evaluations for UK and European government, public bodies and charities. With a growing portfolio we are recruiting for two roles in our Social Policy Directorate.

- A senior quantitative researcher/analyst in our Education, Employment and Skills team delivering impactful evaluation findings concerned with education policy, skills and the labour market.
- A senior quantitative researcher/analyst providing in one of our other Social Policy teams supporting evaluations in areas such as health and social care, environment and the impact of emerging technologies.

This is an opportunity to work on complex, policy-relevant projects that generate robust evidence for decision makers.

- Our Education, Employment and Skills team deliver impact evaluations for clients such as the Department for Education, Youth Endowment Fund and the Education Endowment Fund often combining primary research with secondary analysis of datasets such as the National Pupil Database (NPD) and Individualised Learner Record.
- Our Health and Social Care and Science and Emerging Technology teams deliver flagship evaluations for clients including the Department of Health and Social Care, National Institute of Health Research, the Department for Science and Information Technology as well as UK Research and Innovation funded projects.

For both of these roles, you will combine strong quantitative and analytical capability with effective communication, project management and client engagement skills. The role is suited to a quantitative social science researcher, applied economist or evaluation specialist with strong causal inference skills, and at least five years’ experience delivering comparable evaluation or research projects. You will be confident applying quantitative methods, interpreting findings, and explaining technical approaches clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.

You will also support the development of early career colleagues and help to maintain high standards of quality and methodological rigour across project delivery. You will contribute to competitive tenders for contracts, supporting the development of credible and innovative approaches to policy evaluation requirements.

You will be able to share your thinking and analysis with more qualitative colleagues and work on mixed methods evaluations and research.

Evaluation design and delivery

- Support the design and delivery of proportionate, credible experimental and quasi-experimental impact evaluations of public policies, programmes and interventions.
- Lead analytical workstreams within larger mixed-method evaluations, from design through to reporting.
- Support the interpretation and synthesis of quantitative and qualitative evidence.
- Critically assess assumptions, risks, limitations and the strength of causal claims.
- Lead (desirable) or support (essential) economic evaluation and Value for Money (VfM) assessments with input from subject matter experts.

Quantitative analysis

- Manage, clean, link and analyse complex administrative and survey datasets.
- Apply experimental and quasi-experimental methods, including, where appropriate, randomised controlled trials, matching, difference-in-differences, regression discontinuity, interrupted time series and synthetic control methods.
- Produce transparent, well-documented and reproducible analytical outputs, primarily in R or comparable statistical software (e.g., Stata, Python).

title: Specialist Librarian - Freelance
description:
RAND Europe is an independent, not-for-profit research organisation whose mission is to help improve policy and decision-making through rigorous and independent research and analysis. We benefit the public interest through the impact and wide dissemination of over 200 projects per year. Our work at its most impactful changes policy, practice and process to the benefit of the public good. That is also our organisational mission.

RAND Europe has approximately 200 staff across offices in Cambridge, Brussels, and the Hague. Our staff represents 22 nationalities, speaks over 20 languages and covers 31 academic disciplines. Our multi- and inter-disciplinary approaches to research generate unique perspectives and insights for our wide-ranging government, foundation and other NGO clients.

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Specialist Librarian to join RAND Europe's research support function on a freelance basis, providing specialist library and information services for systematic reviews and other literature reviews.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced research librarian to play a vital and flexible role in supporting high-impact, policy-relevant research, working in close partnership with our multidisciplinary research teams. This would include supporting frameworks such as evidence synthesis for the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, advising on specific literature reviews with direct impact for policy-making. Our projects typically have rapid turnarounds of weeks and months, requiring rapid and flexible support to support delivery of timely and relevant research.

The successful candidate will bring demonstrable expertise in systematic review methodology, comprehensive literature searching, and evidence synthesis best practice, contributing to the rigour and quality of RAND Europe's research outputs. You will be a flexible and collaborative professional who thrives in a dynamic research environment, brings strong technical skills in information discovery and management, and is energised by swift, client-focused research support.

This role will work on an Freelance/Associate basis, which is designed for individuals who provide services to RAND Europe in a self-employed capacity, rather than as members of our employed workforce. The support from the Associate Librarian will be on an on-demand, flexible, and project-specific basis.

Responsibilities

- Design, develop, and execute comprehensive, reproducible literature search strategies for systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid evidence assessments, evidence maps, and other evidence synthesis projects, primarily in the field of health and healthcare
- Support all stages of the evidence synthesis process, including protocol development, development and review of search strategies, and documentation of methodology in line with applicable reporting standards (such as PRISMA)
- Provide expert consultancy and guidance to research teams on systematic and scoping review methods, processes, and tools, including at the proposal development stage
- Conduct searches across a wide range of bibliographic databases (including MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Cochrane Library, PsycINFO, and others) using MeSH, Emtree, Boolean, keyword, and proximity search techniques
- Define and execute 'grey' literature searches across relevant repositories including government and parliamentary publications, clinical guidelines, HTA databases, and international organisation sources
- Evaluate and advise on the appropriate use of AI-assisted and technology-supported tools for evidence synthesis (e.g., Covidence, DistillerSR, Elicit, Rayyan), maintaining a transparent, critical, and methodologically rigorous approach to their application
- Define and maintain bibliographic records using reference management software, including EndNote and Zotero
- Contribute to the training and guidance of research staff on information literacy, literature searching skills, and evidence synthesis methods
- Contribute to the development and improvement of internal guidance, templates, and resources relating to systematic review and evidence synthesis practice

Requirements

Essential

- Postgraduate qualification in library and information science, information management, or a closely related field, ideally from a CILIP-accredited programme or equivalent
- Substantial experience providing library and information services in a research, academic, or health sciences library setting, with direct and demonstrable involvement in systematic review and evidence synthesis work
- Expertise in designing and documenting systematic literature searches, with strong working knowledge of systematic review and evidence synthesis methodology and standards
- Proficiency searching major health and biomedical bibliographic databases (MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, CINAHL) and general academic databases (e.g., Web of Science, Scopus, ProQuest, EBSCOhost platforms)
- Thorough knowledge of relevant reporting guidelines and methodological standards, including PRISMA, PRESS, and Cochrane or JBI methods
- Experience conducting grey literature searches across health-related and public policy domains
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to communicate complex methodological information clearly to non-specialist audiences
- Strong attention to detail, well-developed organisational skills, and the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines in a fast-paced research environment
- Collaborative approach and the ability to build effective working relationships across multidisciplinary teams
- Commitment to evidence synthesis best practices and to the highest professional standards in search strategy development, methodological documentation, and quality assurance

Desirable

- Experience working in a research consultancy, think tank, policy research institute, or equivalent environment
- CILIP membership or chartership (MCLIP or FCLIP), or membership of other relevant professional bodies such as EAHIL or CILIP Health Libraries Group
- Experience with AI-assisted and technology-supported evidence synthesis tools (e.g., Covidence, DistillerSR, Elicit)
- Academic background or professional experience in a health, biomedical, or public health discipline
- Knowledge of health technology assessment (HTA) frameworks, or experience working with or for organisations such as NICE, ECDC, EMA, WHO, or Cochrane
- Experience providing formal or informal training and coaching to researchers on literature searching and evidence synthesis

- Familiarity with research funding and grant proposal processes in a UK or European context

RAND Europe offers a stimulating, intellectually rewarding, and collegial working environment, with competitive remuneration. We work across a wide range of topics and clients, including the UK Government and European Union institutions, and provide an opportunity to engage on an exciting range of topics, tools, and clients.
